title: Visualizing Sigmoid Probabilities and Log-Odds along the Linear Score z
description: Compute z = X_aug @ theta and p = sigmoid(z), plot both true labels and predicted probabilities along the 1D score z, and print the fitted log-odds equation.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Compute each sample's linear score `z = X_aug @ theta` and predicted probability `p = sigmoid(z)`. Build `z_grid` with the supplied point count and `sig_grid = sigmoid(z_grid)`.
Plot the smooth curve `(z_grid, sig_grid)`, scatter the jittered true `0/1` labels `y_bin + jitter` at `z`, and scatter the predicted probabilities `(z, p)` with black `'x'` markers.

Compare the two scatter calls: `y_bin + jitter` shows the binary ground truth near `0` and `1` with small vertical jitter. The jitter keeps overlapping points visible, while `p` sits directly on the sigmoid curve.

steps.question: In the printed equation `log( p / (1 - p) ) = -2.760 + 1.476*x1 + 1.298*x2`, where do the three coefficients come from?
steps.answer: They are the rounded entries of `theta` (`[-2.75992307, 1.47580635, 1.29800476]`): the intercept `theta[0]` followed by the two feature weights `theta[1]` and `theta[2]`.

steps.description: Print `theta` (`[-2.75992307, 1.47580635, 1.29800476]`) and format the linear log-odds equation `log( p / (1 - p) ) = -2.760 + 1.476*x1 + 1.298*x2`.
